body.statement: If \(s_i=\sigma^2\) for every arm, then \(w_i=1/K\), \(C=2(K-1)/K\), \(\eta=1/(K-1)\), \[\rho^\star=\frac{K^2}{2(K-1)^2+K},\qquad G=\frac{2K(K-1)}{2(K-1)^2+K}.\] In particular, \(K=3\) gives \(\rho^\star=9/11\) and \(G=12/11\), recovering the common-variance late-elimination improvement.
body.justification: This mandatory reduction checks the weighted formula against the known symmetric geometry.
body.gap: Imbens, Qin, and Wager establish common-variance dominance; the proposition shows that the new weighted theorem contains that regime rather than replacing it by an analogue on a disjoint class.
body.consumer: Readers can benchmark the heteroskedastic schedule against the familiar equal-allocation design and reproduce the three-arm gain by hand.
